title: Remote Subgraph (using interrupt) not resuming
observed_behavior: A supervisor graph adds a RemoteGraph (a graph served by 'langgraph dev') as node 'child'. The remote graph's node_b calls interrupt(). The interrupt propagates up to the supervisor, but sending Command(resume='...') to the supervisor does not reach the remote graph: it starts a fresh run and re-asks the interrupt instead of continuing.
structure_focus: RemoteGraph compiled subgraph with interrupt; resume Command crossing a deployment boundary (supervisor thread vs remote thread)
notes: Open; a commenter confirms on langgraph 1.2.6 across separately deployed agents. The local-subgraph control in the issue resumes correctly, which is why this is classified framework/platform rather than user graph design. The fixture contains both sides of the reported topology: the remote agent that is served by langgraph dev (not run here) and the supervisor that embeds RemoteGraph and sends Command(resume=...). Running it needs a live langgraph server at REMOTE_URL.
